drug_class: Combination Antihypertensive (ARB + Calcium Channel Blocker + Diuretic)
purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure (hypertension). It combines three different medicines into one tablet to make it easier to manage your blood pressure. Keeping your blood pressure under control helps protect your heart, kidneys, and brain from serious problems like heart attacks and strokes.
how_it_works: Telmisartan relaxes your blood vessels by blocking a hormone that causes them to tighten up. Amlodipine also helps relax and widen your blood vessels by preventing calcium from entering the vessel walls and heart muscle. Indapamide is a mild water pill (diuretic) that helps your kidneys remove extra salt and fluid from your body, which also lowers blood pressure. Together, these three medicines work in different ways to bring your blood pressure down more effectively.
common_side_effects: You may notice dizziness, especially when standing up quickly, so take it slow when getting up. Other common effects include swollen ankles or feet, headache, feeling tired, flushing or warmth in your face, needing to urinate more often (especially at first), and mild stomach upset. Most of these are usually mild and settle down after a few days.
warnings: Do not take this medicine if you are pregnant or planning to become pregnant, as it can seriously harm an unborn baby. Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver problems, low potassium levels, gout, or diabetes. Avoid drinking alcohol as it can cause your blood pressure to drop too low and make you feel dizzy or faint. Do not suddenly stop taking this medicine without talking to your doctor first. Let all your doctors and dentist know you are taking this medication, as it can interact with other medicines including common pain relievers like ibuprofen.
typical_dosing: This medicine is usually taken once a day, at the same time each day, with or without food. Your doctor will prescribe the right strength for you based on your blood pressure and how well you respond to treatment. Always follow your doctor's instructions and never adjust your dose on your own. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember — but if it is almost time for your next dose, just skip the missed one and carry on as normal.
